Yes, shipping test mascaras containing an unlisted color additive to an outside safety lab is permitted under an exemption, provided that the shipment meets specific labeling and recordkeeping requirements. The exemption applies only if the product bears a label stating prominently: “Caution—Contains new color additive—For investigational use only,” and the shipment is delivered by experts qualified to determine safety [1]. This exemption does not apply unless the conditions in §71.37(a) are met, including that no animals used in such investigations or their products (e.g., milk, eggs) shall be used for food purposes without prior authorization from the FDA based on public health data [1].

The labeling required is a prominently displayed statement: “Caution—Contains new color additive—For investigational use only” on the container of the mascara containing the unlisted color additive [1].

The person responsible for shipping or delivering the product must maintain adequate records that include the name and post-office address of the expert to whom the color additive is shipped, the date, quantity, and batch or code mark of each shipment or delivery, and these records must be kept for a period of 2 years after such shipment and delivery [2]. These records must be available for inspection and copying upon request by a properly authorized employee of the FDA at reasonable times [2].
